Odin × Godot

Box3D upstream reuse matrix

12 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Exact source revisionsRuntime and API comparisonAuthoring, resources, and presentationCoordinates and stable identityBuild and export evidenceRecommended reuse boundarymulti-box-3d ownership lessonsPreliminary provenance and unresolved decisions

Source audit recorded October 30, 2026 for board b_cdde1cdfea104035, task t_44f35034af544ab3 (P0.3). This report covers inspected source, build files, manifests, and test definitions. It does not claim that the two Godot integrations were built or their tests passed locally. See upstream-baseline.md for reproduced results and snapshot-audit.md for the snapshot implementation audit.

The best initial reuse candidate is Box3D's C API plus the C snapshot shim from rollback-in-a-box. Keep its network session outside the dependency boundary. Use box3d-godot as the principal editor/custom-node reference and godot-box3d as the stock-node/query compatibility reference. Neither Godot integration currently supplies the ownership and transaction contract required by both Kit and Replay.

Kit and Replay remain sibling frameworks. Replay already implements complete gameplay resimulation and rollback; its missing integration is complete external solver state, not another input, correction, session, or rollback runtime.

Exact source revisions#

The repositories were shallow-cloned into the phase-zero scratch workspace; recorded revisions identify the inspected trees rather than moving branch names.

Repository Inspected commit Relevant dependency boundary
bearlikelion/godot-box3d f073c2de2523bf12163095e920347881352dc8a9 Box3D gitlink 3fc20f5b453ba9e14cdf54ecafa87a2a4bcdf53c; godot-cpp fetched at godot-4.3-stable.
Stink-O/box3d-godot 72bf5f2f9a803e18949507f46dc38916be21ca1c Fork includes the engine tree; godot-cpp gitlink ba0edfed90512ec64aba51d4295a3e7e30112f86. Godot code is under godot/.
pdaddyo/rollback-in-a-box 9e1fe882a0ea4eb52e160d5754a752580b4db462 Setup script pins Box3D d421e45c828f6f853a145f726f0b9425d31146eb and godot-cpp godot-4.5-stable. Core can depend on Box3D alone.
pdaddyo/multi-box-3d 987f4ca44d0065676f17cab35edad57fcbb63b13 Its rollback-in-a-box gitlink is 91e01dc75e8dfe3fbd890f21361e27b31fa2e994, not the current rollback repository revision above.

The different Box3D revisions must not be combined by copying headers or C++ wrappers between projects. In particular, the private snapshot layout is bound to its exact engine revision. P0.4 must record immutable godot-cpp SHAs behind the tags before adopting a build dependency. The fork's in-tree engine is not an independent upstream pin for the Odin spike.

Runtime and API comparison#

Concern godot-box3d box3d-godot rollback-in-a-box
Integration model Implements PhysicsServer3DExtension; registers a selectable physics server. Stock Godot nodes retain their API. Registers custom Node3D, utility, Resource, and replay classes. Separate Box3D world beside Godot physics. Engine-neutral C/C++ simulation and network code with thin Godot and Unreal adapters; also a generated raw Godot binding.
Tick owner Godot invokes server _step, which steps every active space. Box3DWorld defaults to automatic physics processing; manual step(delta) exists. Optional async mode can skip a requested tick while its previous solve remains busy. rb::RollbackWorld::step_frame explicitly invokes b3World_Step with configured fixed step/substeps; rb::RollbackSession can drive it. The public C API can be stepped directly without either class.
Solver snapshots No snapshot/rollback API found in the integration's src/ tree. Recording/player support exists, but the live world API's transform interpolation snapshots are not a complete rollback-world snapshot interface. b3r_create/save/load/destroy, same-context slot buffers, plus wrapper side-state; uses private Box3D snapshot machinery. See the separate audit for its omissions and restore failure behavior.
Shapes Sphere, box, capsule, cylinder, convex/concave polygon, heightmap, boundary, and query-only separation-ray implementations. Body authors sphere/capsule/hull/mesh/heightfield/compound geometry; child shapes author box, sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone. Box/cylinder/cone become hull geometry. Raw API includes Box3D geometry families. Convenience RollbackWorld only creates static/dynamic boxes, spheres, and capsules; it is not the full raw API.
Joints Pin, hinge, slider, and internal filter joint. ConeTwist and Generic6DOF entry points explicitly reject unsupported operations. Nine custom joint classes: hinge, slider, distance, ball, fixed, motor, wheel, parallel, filter. Some authoring behavior creates companion constraints. Raw generated API reaches all native joint families. RollbackWorld convenience class does not supply a comparable authoring surface.
Queries and characters Implements direct-space and direct-body Godot APIs, motion recovery/casts, and stock CharacterBody3D behavior. Custom world/body/collision query APIs and a custom kinematic capsule character node. Results commonly contain Godot objects resolved from native userData. Native Box3D C queries are available; generated Godot dispatch is a separate scripting layer. No replacement for Replay's existing game query/input/presentation model.
Live identity Godot RID ownership plus C++ object pointers in native body userData. Nodes retain raw body/shape/joint handles; bodies, child shapes, and joints put Godot node pointers in userData. Wrapper uses packed native body IDs and slot-copied side tables. Raw IDs are explicitly distinguished from game entity IDs.

Source entry points:

  • PhysicsServer registration and stepping: register_types.cpp, Box3DPhysicsServer3D::_step, Box3DSpace3D::step.
  • Custom world scheduling and side effects: Box3DWorld::step, Box3DBody::create_body, register_types.cpp.
  • Neutral core: core/CMakeLists.txt, rollback_shim.h, RollbackWorld, IRollbackSimulation.

Authoring, resources, and presentation#

box3d-godot is the stronger reference for custom editor UX. It registers collider and joint gizmo plugins at editor initialization only, supplies class documentation and node icons, and draws geometry/constraint previews. Box3DBody::create_baked_compound assembles child geometry into one static compound with geometry deduplication. The bake has meaningful limitations: per-child filters/events no longer survive as separate solver shapes, and child shape IDs/live mutators are unavailable for the baked representation. Its geometry utility layer converts procedural engine geometry into owned Godot arrays without leaking temporary native allocations. These are useful patterns for immutable shape definitions and editor validation.

This does not establish the proposed durable authoring asset contract. The inspected implementation primarily authors node properties and builds native geometry; it is not a reusable suite of stable-ID, versioned box/sphere/hull/mesh/heightfield Resource definitions. No EditorImportPlugin or GLTFDocumentExtension implementation, or general durable entity/shape ID bake, was located in godot/src/. Its contact-rule Resource and recording objects serve different purposes. Odin's eventual baker must define deterministic traversal, stable content IDs, serializer versions, source mesh identity, scale validation, and native geometry lifetime.

Useful source references are box3d_editor_gizmos.cpp, box3d_body.h, Box3DBody bake documentation, and Box3DGeometry.

godot-box3d instead translates stock shape resources into backend implementations. Its shape update/lifecycle tests and motion-recovery/query algorithms are useful compatibility references; the integration has no separate custom authoring/import/gizmo layer in src/. Existing stock-node editor behavior should not be mistaken for a rollback-aware baking pipeline. Its behavior differences document query-only separation rays, sensor/concave restrictions, convex query requirements, material mixing differences, and ignored joint parameters. Carry these cases into any later compatibility tests instead of assuming matching method names imply matching behavior.

For runtime resimulation, neither node layer should directly become canonical physics state. The custom world synchronizes nodes before/after stepping and dispatches contact, sensor, joint, and body signals. Its async path deliberately trades tick progress for smooth rendering. The PhysicsServer layer performs Godot callbacks and caches contacts after each solve. Those policies need separation from a fixed, exactly replayed simulation step. Reuse geometry, gizmo, conversion, and query ideas while emitting framework events and reading presentation copies through each sibling's own adapter.

Coordinates and stable identity#

Both bindings map vectors directly between Godot and Box3D. The custom-node binding explicitly uses Godot's Y-up/right-handed convention; quaternion conversion maps (x, y, z, w) to Box3D's vector/scalar representation. Scale is baked into geometry rather than represented in the rigid-body transform. The PhysicsServer implementation forces single-precision Box3D in CMake; its conversion header assumes that choice. Both integrations expose the process-wide length-units setting. Adopt one explicit convention and initialize it before any world/geometry creation; do not assume independent per-world length units. See box3d_conversions.h, type_conversions.hpp, and box3d_globals.cpp.

Native body handles, RIDs, node pointers, ObjectIDs, and scene paths are runtime references, not durable game identity. A restored solver must restore the logical entity-to-body mapping and rebind callback/presentation references. Snapshot-era native handle behavior does not make a handle created after the restored tick valid, nor make a handle portable to another world or machine. The existing shim's pointer clearing makes direct reuse of the bindings' userData event routing especially unsuitable without an explicit rebind step.

Build and export evidence#

Project Source-defined build/export surface What remains unverified here
godot-box3d CMake 3.22, C++17 wrapper, separate Box3D submodule; godot-cpp ExternalProject pinned by tag. Forces Box3D single precision. MinGW statically links runtime; Linux hides linked static symbols. GDExtension minimum 4.3, with Linux/Windows x86-64 and macOS library entries. CI defines Linux/Windows headless tests and macOS build. No local build/test was run for this matrix. macOS runtime behavior, alternate architectures, web/mobile export and rollback integration are not established.
box3d-godot godot/SConstruct compiles the C17 engine and C++ wrappers into one extension using godot-cpp, targets API 4.6. Manifest lists desktop, Android arm64/x86-64 and threaded release WASM. macOS workflow defines universal builds and headless checks against 4.7.1/4.6.3 and Rosetta. Web adds SIMD flags; no-thread build disables asynchronous stepping. Source-defined packaging or a workflow is not a local passing result. The README explicitly leaves WASM determinism unverified. Export ability does not establish cross-target rollback identity.
rollback-in-a-box Neutral static core needs only a Box3D CMake target and uses C17/C++17. Godot build adds godot-cpp and adapter objects. Simulation compiler flags disable FP contraction on GCC/Clang and request precise FP on MSVC. Manifest lists macOS arm64 and Linux/Windows x86-64, minimum Godot 4.5. P0.1 owns local build/test results. No WASM/mobile adapter/export or cross-target identity is established by the inspected manifest. A fingerprint/probe is a compatibility diagnostic, not proof for every game/corpus.

Build references: godot-box3d/CMakeLists.txt, ExternalGodotCpp.cmake, box3d-godot/SConstruct, custom-node manifest, macOS workflow, and neutral core build.

The Odin integration should compile one pinned engine plus its compatibility shim, avoiding multiple Box3D copies with separate global settings/world ID domains. A C-only snapshot target is narrower than the current neutral CMake target, which also compiles rb_world.cpp and rb_session.cpp. Consuming the entire Godot object target unnecessarily adds godot-cpp registration and the upstream session. Existing Odin native/WASM build composition still needs its own explicit link/export work and verification.

Recommended reuse boundary#

Candidate Initial disposition Work before adoption
Pinned Box3D public C headers/library Runtime dependency candidate. Minimal typed Odin bindings or C wrappers; ABI/layout checks, exact precision/SIMD/compiler configuration, lifecycle/query tests, and license record.
core/src/rollback_shim.c and its C header Small compatibility-code reuse candidate, subject to P0.2/P0.4. Isolate private-header dependency; repair/extend ownership, failure, lifetime, and hash contracts needed by the siblings. Keep an upgrade audit.
rb::RollbackWorld Reference for fixed stepping and solver-plus-side-state save/load; optional C++ helper only if justified. It is noncopyable, vector-owning C++, not a C/Odin value-frame API. It provides limited convenience bodies and a body-oriented diagnostic hash, not a general complete-state codec.
rb::RollbackSession and Godot reflection bridge Keep outside the runtime dependency boundary. Kit and Replay already own input/prediction/session/replay policy. Importing this peer session would introduce another authority and history contract.
Raw binding generator/API manifest Reference/checking input. It generates Godot Variant/GDScript dispatch, not Odin declarations. Reuse the coverage method or adapt only needed parsing after attribution review. Avoid a Godot scripting bridge in a native Odin call path.
Custom-node geometry, gizmos, joint/query patterns Editor/API references; selectively port after Gate B. Separate immutable authored definitions from runtime handles and Godot callbacks; define stable IDs and versioned baking; test against the chosen engine pin.
PhysicsServer motion/query/filter and stock shape lifecycle Compatibility references. Preserve documented behavior differences. A full stock-node backend remains a separate project; do not make it a prerequisite for the rollback spike.
multi-box-3d side-state and lifecycle scenarios Behavioral/test reference. Keep game rules outside the shared backend. Do not copy its game code until P0.4 resolves missing root licensing. Reproduce at its own gitlink before considering upgrades.

The initial C boundary should expose world/body/shape lifecycle and explicit step through Box3D's public API, and a narrow opaque snapshot owner through the shim. Add bounded array query/event adapters only where direct C callbacks would make lifetime or thread ownership ambiguous. C++ classes, std::vector, Godot Variant/objects, and upstream session packets should not cross the Odin boundary.

The existing snapshot owner is not yet a ready-made Replay Frame field. It binds slots and a geometry registry to one live world/context; it supplies no detached retain/release or import-into-another-world contract. P0.0/P0.2 must choose how the framework owns snapshots and how staged correction, audit, aborts, eviction, copied frames, and canonical recovery preserve complete state. A copied slot index or hidden live-world pointer is insufficient.

For hash diagnostics, inspect actual coverage rather than relying on the word "world": b3r_world_hash delegates to the engine's state hash, while RollbackWorld::state_hash_u64 adds frame/body mapping/render metadata. P0.2 must identify solver and side-state omissions before this becomes the confirmed complete-state comparison used by either adapter. Current geometry interning also means the August issue's collision-mesh duplication warning is historical context, not evidence that every current snapshot copies all geometry.

multi-box-3d ownership lessons#

The game embeds a rollback extension object target in its existing GDExtension, keeping one engine and one registration context. Its own Box3DWorld supplies the simulation interface and saves game side-state beside physics: frame/spawn counters, players, body tables, entities, vehicles, creatures/droids, wave RNG and timers. load_state restores those values and rebuilds derived reverse maps. Terrain/vehicle definitions are explicitly immutable during the match; their lifetime still outlives live/restored shapes. Physics recording is kept outside rollback.

These boundaries are useful references for both siblings, but the game's render table is not a prescribed canonical field for Odin. Each framework should classify its own complete deterministic side-state and presentation metadata. See ROLLBACK_EXTENSION.md, SideState, and save_state/load_state.

The current game pins an older rollback revision. Its documented embedding link list includes godot-cpp and box3d; the current neutral extraction adds a separate box3d_rollback_neutral target. Therefore an upgrade must review link dependencies as well as the API and snapshots; silently advancing the gitlink would cease to reproduce the recorded game source.

Preliminary provenance and unresolved decisions#

The inspected godot-box3d root LICENSE is MIT, copyright Mark Arneman; rollback-in-a-box root LICENSE is MIT, copyright Paul Barrass. The custom-node fork's root LICENSE names Erin Catto; its Godot source headers use contributor MIT SPDX declarations, and its packaged addon LICENSE explicitly attributes the extension to Stink-O and the engine to Erin Catto. Preserve all applicable notices for any reused source and dependencies; P0.4 owns the final attribution inventory and reuse decision.

No root LICENSE, COPYING, or NOTICE was located in the inspected multi-box-3d tracked tree; its GodotSteam addon has a separate license that does not establish the game code's license. Treat game source as reference only until that gap is resolved. This report does not vendor or copy upstream implementation code.

Source notices: godot-box3d/LICENSE, rollback-in-a-box/LICENSE, fork/LICENSE, and packaged addon LICENSE.

Before P0.5, combine this matrix with snapshot findings and reproduced baseline results to select the pin and minimal reused files. Resolve detached snapshot ownership/transactions, complete hash coverage, canonical recovery, geometry registry lifetime/memory caps, callback rebinds, and the first desktop/CI pair. Keep the initial spike independent of editor work and leave platform-wide determinism claims to measured target-specific corpora.
